summary: Moorpark sits in a narrow east-west valley between the Santa Susana Mountains and the Tierra Rejada hills, which means most of its 12.5 square miles slope upward toward golden-grass ridgelines visible from practically every parking lot — and those ridgelines light up a deep amber at sunset roughly 290 days a year, thanks to an annual average of 9.7 hours of sunshine per day and mild lows around 55°F. Despite being part of Ventura County, this is functionally a bedroom community tethered to the 118 and 23 freeways; Amgen's Thousand Oaks campus and the broader Conejo Valley employment corridor sit just over the southern hills, while commuters heading to the San Fernando Valley face a winding but scenic 20-mile run through the Santa Susana Pass. The home-price-to-income ratio lands around 5.7×, which is steep but notably less crushing than neighboring Thousand Oaks or Simi Valley relative to local earnings, and a 4.5% poverty rate signals the economic base is solid. Moorpark College, a well-enrolled community college with a teaching zoo that actually trains exotic-animal keepers, anchors the town's western end and gives the place a mild institutional identity beyond pure residential subdivision. The food and retail scene is mostly freeway-adjacent strip centers rather than a cohesive downtown — you drive to eat, you drive to shop — but open-space preserves in the surrounding hills put genuine trail access within a short trip from most neighborhoods. Moorpark is the rare Southern California suburb where the landscape dramatically outperforms the streetscape.
